newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor plans stadium guarantee-report.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor plans stadium guarantee-report.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown will unveil an agreement on Tuesday that would guarantee the city never has to dip into its general fund to pay off bonds for a proposed stadium-mall complex, according to a published report.

San Francisco residents on June 3 will vote on a $100 million lease revenue bond measure that would help to finance the city's share of the proposed $525 million San Francisco 49ers football stadium and shopping complex.
Facing a tough fight to win approval for the bond measure, Brown will announce his plan to protect the city's general fund at a press conference Tuesday, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.
Sources told the Chronicle that the guarantee will be provided by Morgan Stanley Group Inc, which will take a lead role in securing the project's private financing.

Under the agreement, the firm would buy an insurance policy guaranteeing that the city's general fund would remain untouched if tax revenues generated by the project fell below projections, the Chronicle reported.
City officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
